text:
maria (arch): quick RFC follow-up: proposing an "in-place dedupe" upgrade flow for onprem model stores where delta bundles create new objects and then swap symlinks to avoid full-copy activation. concerns: GC safety during partial apply, operator rollback UX, and how verifier/attestation fits. sketch below.

alex (eng-runtime): I like minimizing disk churn. are we assuming content-addressed objects (sha256) and symlinks per-model-version?

maria (arch): yes. idea: bundle contains new objects + a manifest that references them by digest. operator uploads bundle to a staging area, verifier attests signatures, then we create objects in store and atomically swap model symlink from old root to new root.

vanessa (eng-ops): how do we prevent the old objects from being GC'd while some nodes are still serving the old root? nodes may stream long-lived connections.

maria (arch): plan: add an activation lease: when we swap symlink we record an activation epoch (timestamp + TTL). nodes will renew leases while they hold KV caches for old root. GC only collects objects whose epoch < lowest active lease.

jules (security): leases look fine but need to ensure attestation of the manifest is tied to the activation record so an operator cannot swap unverified manifests. also need audit trail for who triggered activation.

alex (eng-runtime): runtime change: on apply, create a small activation-record file under /var/lib/modelstore/activations/<epoch>.json containing {root:,manifest_digest:,signed_by:}, and each runtime process reads the activation table and pins referenced objects for its TTL. renewal via a lightweight heartbeat to local operator socket.

upgrade-bot: deployment rollback recorded: 6723400123 by tom (sre) — reason: failed shard checksum on node 12

tom (sre): that rollback event shows why we need fast diff apply. if shard checksums mismatch we need a reversible path: swap back symlink to previous root and avoid double-delete race on objects that are shared between versions.

vanessa (eng-ops): operational playbook: 1) upload bundle to staging 2) verifier checks signatures 3) create objects (CAS) 4) dry-apply on subset of nodes (canary) 5) swap activation symlink 6) monitor leases and metrics 7) final GC after leases expire. need commands for dry-apply and forced rollback.

maria (arch): proposed CLI ext: `redwood onprem apply --bundle BUNDLE.tar --canary 10% --dry-run` and `redwood onprem rollback --epoch <epoch> --force`

alex (eng-runtime): note: for low-disk nodes we should prefer hardlinks/symlinks over copies; but hardlinks can't cross filesystems. fallback: store objects in content-addressed store that supports reflinks where available. runtime must detect copy-on-write support.

jules (security): also add HSM-stored signing keys for operator-level approvals; make `--force` require explicit two-party consent or a bypass token logged in audit.

vanessa (eng-ops): what about partial object apply failures? e.g., upload interrupts leaving a subset of objects present. we need a resume mechanism and idempotent apply steps.

maria (arch): apply should be idempotent: objects are written by digest name; upload step is `put-object(digest)` that is safe to retry. we keep a per-bundle manifest file with an `apply_state` (uploaded/canary/activated/rolledback) guarded by operator-level CAS to avoid double activation.

alex (eng-runtime): runtime GC algorithm suggestion: GC range scan respects activation epochs. Pseudocode: ```for obj in store: if lowest_active_epoch <= obj.epoch_marker: skip else if obj.ref_count==0: delete``` This requires keeping per-object epoch_marker (first-introduced-epoch).

tom (sre): monitoring: expose `modelstore.active_epochs`, `modelstore.leases`, and `modelstore.orphan_candidates`. add alert when orphan_candidates growth > X for Y minutes.

vanessa (eng-ops): UX: operator wants a preview of disk delta before activation: `redwood onprem preview-delta --bundle BUNDLE.tar` prints estimated new bytes, shared-bytes, and worst-case peak disk.

maria (arch): agreed. final open questions: - how long should default lease TTL be? (30m vs 6h) - operator CLIs vs console hooks for manual approval - offline airgap: how do we transfer activation records when no control-plane access? suggestion: include activation manifest in bundle and require operator to place a signed activation token on a bastion.

jules (security): TTL default should be conservative for long lived streams; propose 2h default and make it configurable per-apply. for airgap, signed activation token + offline verifier is adequate if operator signs.

alex (eng-runtime): perf note: symlink swap is cheap but many small files can make listing slow; we should keep manifests hierarchical (shard buckets) and support indexed manifests to avoid full-listing on activation.

maria (arch): thanks all. I'll update the RFC with: activation leases, per-bundle apply_state, preview CLI, resumable CAS upload, and GC respecting lowest active epoch. I'll also add the airgap activation token flow and two-party rollback guard. tagging follow-ups: @alex for runtime impl notes, @vanessa for playbook steps, @jules for signing requirements. :thumbsup:
